audit.why: Difficulty 4/10 FAVOURED matches the 50.69% win rate over 2752 games for a melee diver into an immobile mage with one zoning tool; early and mid lane are Irelia's, side lane and teamfights stay hers because Viktor has no dash and no self-peel.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text was written around 'Hex Core' and an 'E upgrade from Hex Core', which is not what the kit describes. Riot's text is Glorious Evolution granting Hex Fragments that augment individual abilities.
audit.why: Fabricated/outdated system name in three of four spikes plus the Level 6 spike calling the ultimate 'Chaos Storm' instead of Arcane Storm.
audit.corrected: Spikes rewritten to Glorious Evolution / Hex Fragments and Arcane Storm, with real cooldowns: Hextech Ray 12/11/10/9/8s, Gravity Field 17/16/15/14/13s, Arcane Storm 120/100/80s. Irelia's own spikes: level 3 (E online), level 6 Vanguard's Edge, first item.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three applicable interactions were absent: Arcane Storm (R) is a channel and Flawless Duet (E) cancels it; Siphon Power (Q) grants a shield that eats the burst window; Siphon Power is an auto-attack reset, so the wind-up is the tell.
audit.why: These are the decisive mechanical facts of the matchup and none of them reached the page.
audit.corrected: R-cancel written into dosFull[2].d, whys[4] and spikes[1].text; the Siphon Power shield written into spikes[2].text and enemyWin.

audit.why: It is the field that carries real cooldowns.
audit.corrected: Gravity Field 17s at rank 1 to 13s at rank 5; Hextech Ray 12s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was the tradeBad string verbatim (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED).
audit.why: Body did not match the title.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten to match their titles: passive stacking before commits, and what shoving the wave costs.

edits.before: - Viktor Gravity Field: matchup-defining — The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget W Defiant Dance for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Gravity Field (W) is 17s at rank 1, 13s at rank 5 — it slows first and only stuns if you linger, so walk sideways out and step up the moment it is spent. - Hextech Ray (E) sits down 12s at rank 1: that is your commit window.

edits.before: Q-reset through two low minions onto his chest, four-stack autos, E-stun the retreat — the wave-funded all-in he budgeted zero for.
edits.after: Bladesurge (Q) and Flawless Duet (E) each stack the passive; arrive at four before you touch him, or bonus on-hit damage never funds the kill.

edits.before: Dashing in under-stacked with W down — Irelia without the engine is a melee minion with a famous haircut.
edits.after: Every low minion is a Bladesurge charge; shove them into his tower and you hand him a lane with no dash targets.

edits.before: Viktor whiffs Gravity Field and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Arcane Storm (R) is a channel — Flawless Duet's stun kills it.

edits.before: The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Bladesurge refreshes on kill, so a wave of low minions is a free path to his face — 600 range per hop, no cooldown spent.

edits.before: Viktor wins by landing Gravity Field, denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Viktor wins by stunning you inside Gravity Field, shielding your burst with Siphon Power, and farming Hex Fragments.

edits.before: Carry through the dance — the wave funds dives no cooldown can, and your R turns skirmishes into no-exit interviews.
edits.after: Carry by hunting him: he has no dash, so Bladesurge resets off low minions put you on his chest and Vanguard's Edge seals it.

edits.before: Ahead, dance louder: crash waves into Viktor's face, stun the answers, and surf resets through every river fight.
edits.after: Ahead, keep him off the wave: Hex Fragments come from kills, so freeze him out and punish every step up with a reset dash.

edits.before: Chaos Storm needs setup you can dodge by engaging from an unexpected angle
edits.after: Arcane Storm is a channel — your Flawless Duet stun cancels it outright

edits.before: Before Viktor gets his E upgrade from Hex Core, his kit has almost no way to stop your dash-ins, so all-in whenever Gravity Field isn't blocking your path.
edits.after: Before Glorious Evolution augments his abilities, nothing in his kit stops a dash — Gravity Field slows on entry and only stuns if you stand in it, so cross it.

edits.before: Chaos Storm punishes overextending during the pull, so dash in from an angle Gravity Field can't zone and burst him before the storm lands.
edits.after: Arcane Storm is a channel: hold Flawless Duet for the cast and its stun cancels the storm, then Vanguard's Edge walls off his retreat.

edits.before: Trinity Force or Sunderer closes the damage gap on his Hex Core stacks and lets you kill him in one dash-reset combo before he can kite with E.
edits.after: Blade of the Ruined King closes the gap on his evolved abilities: four stacks plus a Bladesurge reset kills him through the Siphon Power shield.

edits.before: Fully stacked Hex Core Viktor with augmented E can zone you hard, so time your engages around his E cooldown rather than walking into laser range.
edits.after: Augmented Hextech Ray adds an explosion behind the beam, and at rank 5 it is only 8s down — engage on the cast, not into the 525-range line.

notes: Level chart is Irelia 7/7 while the win rate is 50.69% over 2752 games. The kit supports Irelia winning every lane stage (Viktor has no dash and no self-peel), so the rows were left alone rather than half-moved; the flatness is likely a scaling artefact, not a lane one. 'Chaos Storm' and 'Hex Core' appeared throughout the content layer — both replaced with Riot's current names (Arcane Storm, Glorious Evolution / Hex Fragments). Item advice disagrees across layers: report[8] says Blade of the Ruined King / on-hit, spikes[2] said Trinity Force or Sunderer; spikes[2] aligned to the on-hit line.
